algorithm_plan.description: Validate supply vector, demand vector, and cost_matrix inputs against declared contract: supply and demand must be non-empty non-negative finite float64 sequences; cost_matrix must have shape (len(supply), len(demand)) with non-negative finite float64 entries. No transport distance computation performed at this step.

Define balance check topology: compute sum(supply) and sum(demand) in canonical left-to-right order using float64 accumulation. Verify |sum(supply) - sum(demand)| <= declared relative balance tolerance (e.g., 1e-9 * max(sum(supply), sum(demand))). Unbalanced inputs must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE. No LP invoked at this step.

Define cost matrix validation topology: verify cost_matrix shape is exactly (m, n) where m = len(supply) and n = len(demand); verify all cost values are non-negative finite float64. Shape mismatch or invalid cost values must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE. Cost matrix is stored row-major in canonical JSON array-of-arrays format. No LP invoked at this step.

Define closed-form degenerate path topology for cases requiring no LP: for m=1 (single source), the transport distance equals sum_j cost_matrix[0][j] * demand[j] in left-to-right order; for n=1 (single target), the transport distance equals sum_i cost_matrix[i][0] * supply[i] in left-to-right order; for the 1×1 case (m=1, n=1), the transport distance equals cost_matrix[0][0] * supply[0]. These paths are closed-form float64 weighted sums; no LP solver is involved.

Define general m×n LP topology for non-degenerate balanced transport: the LP has m*n non-negative decision variables T[i,j]; m row marginal constraints (T @ 1_n = supply); n column marginal constraints (T^T @ 1_m = demand); objective is minimize sum_{i,j} cost_matrix[i,j] * T[i,j]. LP solver variant, pivot rule, and tie-breaking strategy are declared as planned-only; no LP solver is invoked at this step or in this bundle.

Define all NOT_COMPUTABLE detection branches: empty supply (m=0) or demand (n=0); unbalanced transport (|sum(supply)-sum(demand)| exceeds tolerance); negative supply or demand element; negative cost element; non-finite value in supply, demand, or cost_matrix; cost_matrix shape mismatch. Each condition must route to a documented NOT_COMPUTABLE state without emitting a transport distance value.

Define baseline comparator topology: compare future computed transport distance against expected_transport_distance fields in valid fixture records. For degenerate closed-form cases (m=1, n=1, 1×1), tolerance is zero for exact float64 weighted-sum results. For general LP cases, the declared balance tolerance also governs the comparison policy. No computation or comparison executed at this step.

numerical_stability_plan.description: Float64 required for all supply/demand accumulation, cost accumulation, LP dual variable computation, and comparator arithmetic. Float32 excluded per readiness dossier numerical constraints.
numerical_stability_plan.planned_guardrail: Require float64 precision declaration; reject float32 inputs at validation boundary.

numerical_stability_plan.description: Supply-demand balance check uses a relative tolerance declared as epsilon_rel = 1e-9 * max(sum(supply), sum(demand)). This value is fixed before implementation. Float64 drift in summation of non-trivial supply/demand vectors may produce apparent imbalance; the tolerance prevents spurious NOT_COMPUTABLE.
numerical_stability_plan.planned_guardrail: Declare balance tolerance = 1e-9 relative to the larger total; test fixtures must include a near-tolerance boundary case.

numerical_stability_plan.description: Cost matrix is stored row-major as a JSON array-of-arrays of float64 values. Zero cost values are valid and must not trigger division-by-zero in any comparator. Very large cost values may cause float64 overflow in objective accumulation; declared input magnitude bound required before implementation.
numerical_stability_plan.planned_guardrail: Declare maximum allowed cost value and maximum m*n problem size in the implementation plan; add NOT_COMPUTABLE branch for oversized inputs or cost overflow.

numerical_stability_plan.description: Non-finite float64 values (NaN or infinite) in supply, demand, or cost_matrix must be detected at input validation and produce NOT_COMPUTABLE without any transport distance computation. NaN propagation through cost accumulation is explicitly excluded.
numerical_stability_plan.planned_guardrail: Scan for non-finite values at input validation; route to not-computable state before any accumulation or LP declaration.

numerical_stability_plan.description: The LP solver variant (e.g., simplex with fixed pivot rule), tie-breaking strategy for degenerate problems (multiple optimal transport plans), and iteration limit must be declared and fixed before any implementation PR may be opened. Stochastic LP variants and randomized pivot rules are excluded. LP solver is not invoked in this planning bundle.
numerical_stability_plan.planned_guardrail: Declare solver variant, pivot rule, and tie-breaking rule in the implementation plan before implementation begins; restrict initial test fixtures to problems with unique optimal plans.

numerical_stability_plan.description: Define all conditions under which NOT_COMPUTABLE is the correct output: empty supply or demand, unbalanced transport, negative supply/demand/cost element, non-finite value, cost_matrix shape mismatch. Ensure no silent fallback to a numeric transport distance value.
numerical_stability_plan.planned_guardrail: Enumerate all NOT_COMPUTABLE branches in algorithm topology before implementation; validate each branch has a dedicated test fixture planned.
